source_title: wexloops/openfield: Open-source studio for video, stills and 3D on your own GPU through ComfyUI - GitHub
source_excerpt:
OpenField is an open-source studio for video, stills and 3D that runs on your own GPU through ComfyUI. Every app is a ComfyUI workflow with a screen on top, built on open-weights models and the Comfy SDK.
Built for Comfy's Open Source Higgsfield competition. MIT licensed.
Video : text or an image to video, 28 motion presets, start and end frames, batch takes.
Image : stills from a prompt, animated in one click. On FLUX.2, up to six reference pictures (or @cast ) carry faces, clothes and objects into a new photograph.
Seamless Loop : one image becomes a loop whose first and last frames match.
Object : one still becomes a textured 3D model (GLB with PBR maps and a turntable).
Add sound : a soundtrack for a silent take, with the picture left as it is.
Director : genre, camera, framing, light, film stock, look, grade, an era scrubber (1960 to 2020) and speed ramps compile into the shot.
Scene : write a scene, a local LLM plans 2 to 6 shots, and they render and cut into one take.
Stage : block a shot in 3D with boxes, figures, walls or your own .glb models and a camera path; it renders as a finished shot that moves like the blocking. Figures hold their marks, so write people standing, turning or gesturing where you placed them.
Cast : save a character, prop or place once and @mention it in any prompt.
Your LoRAs : add up to four of your own LoRAs (a character, a style, a motion) to Image or Video. Drop the file in ComfyUI's models/loras ; OpenField reads each file's tensor keys and only offers it to the model it was trained for.
Coverage , Push in , Next beat : nine shots of one moment, a stepped push in, four continuations.
Mirror : film a move on your phone and put that motion onto any character. Restyle (22 looks) and an experimental Object swap.
Reshoot : re-aim the camera on an existing clip after the fact.
Effects : one-click effects on a clip (Cutout, Flood, Nightfall, Empty the scene) or a still (Living photo, Pop, Inflate, Cake, Squish, Unzip, Gulp).
Edit , New angle , Relight , Expand : change a still with a sentence and a mask, see it from new angles, move the light, grow the frame.
Remove background : transparent PNG for stills, ProRes 4444 with alpha for clips.
Speak : a face and a voice track become a talking shot.
Upscale : Sharpen (fast 2x, optional frame doubling), Redraw (SeedVR2 to 1080p or 1440p) or Dream (prompt-steered 2x), with a drag compare.
Extend and Transitions : continue a take or add a lead-in; bridge two takes with a generated move.
Finish in HDR : ACEScg EXR, HLG HEVC and HLG ProRes masters, frame-locked to the source.
Improve the seam : every loop gets a seam score; the fixer trims, re-renders or reseeds.
MCP : 31 tools let Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any MCP client run every app.
Open in ComfyUI : every take opens as the exact workflow that rendered it, or downloads as JSON.
workflows/ : every app's graph committed as API-format JSON.
Phone to Mirror. Scan a QR code, film a move on your phone, and the clip lands in Mirror as the motion source.
Reshoot after the fact. Move the camera on a clip you already have.
Seamless loops with a seam meter. Every loop is measured at its wrap and badged Seamless or Visible seam; the fixer reports the before and after numbers.
Every take opens as its ComfyUI workflow. Download it or open it in ComfyUI, change it, run it there.
HDR and EXR finish. 16-bit half ACEScg EXR sequences and HLG BT.2020 masters.
All local. Renders run on your GPU and land in your folders. No credits, no paid account, no upload. A free Hugging Face account and read token fetch the gated LTX-2.5 weights.
Stage, greybox to shot. Block boxes, figures, props and your own .glb models in the browser, set a lens and a camera path, and the LTX-2.5 Layout-to-Render IC-LoRA renders a finished shot that follows the blocking exactly.
MCP for agents. 31 tools let an agent direct, render, check and finish shots end to end on your machine.
Stage blocks the shot in the browser: boxes, figures, walls, your own .glb models, a lens and a camera path, drawn with three.js. No 3D package is needed. The browser renders two passes of the blocking, a grey clay clip and an exact depth pass from the same camera. The look frame is painted on that depth pass (Z-Image Turbo with the Fun ControlNet Union), so the art-directed still keeps every object where it was blocked. The clay clip and the look frame then go to the LTX-2.5 Layout-to-Render IC-LoRA, which renders a shot that moves like the blocking. Every step runs on open weights on your own GPU.
Every render goes through the official Comfy SDK ( @comfyorg/sdk , server/engine.ts ): asset upload, job submit, the live event stream with step progress and latent previews, outputs and cancel.
Locally the SDK talks to comfy-api-proxy in front of your ComfyUI. OpenField starts the proxy for you.
Local ComfyUI is the supported path. Comfy Cloud is experimental: set COMFY_BASE_URL and COMFY_API_KEY and the same SDK calls go there, but it is untested, the custom node packs limit which apps run, and Object and Finish in HDR need a local engine.
Each app's workflow is a TypeScript graph builder in server/graphs/ . npm run workflows exports them to workflows/ .
Model health and install checks read the ComfyUI server API directly, because Comfy API v2 has no node introspection yet.
Disk per bundle (from server/models.ts ; install only what you use):
dream and ltx-tools add no weights. The Scene planner uses the Gemma 3 12B encoder from the legacy ltx23 bundle when it is present, and falls back to Ollama or a sentence split.
Start ComfyUI (0.38+) with live previews and leave it running: python main.py --listen 127.0.0.1 --port 8188 --preview-method auto
Install OpenField and the Comfy API v2 bridge: git clone https://github.com/wexloops/openfield.git cd openfield npm install pipx install comfy-api-proxy # or a venv; then set COMFY_PROXY_BIN cp .env.example .env
Accept the license at https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5 (and the separately gated LoRA repos if you want Effects, Stage, Cast, HDR or Object swap), create a read token, and put these in .env : HF_TOKEN=hf_... COMFY_MODELS_DIR=/path/to/ComfyUI/models
Fetch the models, restart ComfyUI, check, run: npm run models -- --list # what you have, what you are missing npm run models # core weights: LTX-2.5 + Qwen-Image npm run doctor # checks everything that breaks npm run dev # open http://localhost:3160
For a quick test, open Image and pick Draft .
For one process serving the UI and API together on :3161, run npm run build then npm start .
The full walkthrough, the custom node packs each app needs and every bundle are in docs/INSTALL.md . With Claude Code, open the repo and say "set up OpenField": CLAUDE.md is the install as an agent checklist. One command does it on Linux or WSL: bash scripts/install.sh (see One-command install ; a password-gated preview on a rented GPU is in docs/RUNPOD.md ).
OpenField's code is MIT. It ships no model weights; you download them from their publishers and each keeps its own license. Every default model is open weights.
LTX-2.5 and the LTX IC-LoRAs (video, Stage, Mirror, Reshoot, Effects, HDR): LTX-2.x Community License, free for commercial use under $10M yearly revenue.
Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-Edit 2509, Z-Image Turbo, SeedVR2: Apache 2.0.
TRELLIS.2, BiRefNet, MoGe-2, RealESRGAN, RIFE: MIT or BSD-3-Clause.
DINOv3 and SAM 3.1: Meta licenses, commercial use allowed with acceptable-use exclusions.
Opt-in and non-commercial: FLUX.2 dev and 4x-UltraSharp.
Opt-in and geo-restricted: MiniMax H3 is unlicensed in the US, EU, UK and South Korea. Off by default.
Every model, LoRA and node pack with its license and source is in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md . File lists and sizes are in docs/MODELS.md .
All sample media in this repository was generated with OpenField on open weights. No real people, no third-party footage. Take, prompt, seed and model for every file are in docs/MEDIA.md .
With the OpenField server running, ask in plain words: "Make a 5 second dolly shot of a lighthouse at dusk, then upscale the best take." Claude Desktop setup, the tool list and example prompts are in docs/MCP.md .
All optional, in .env (see .env.example ):
Write a graph builder in server/graphs/ (an API-format ComfyUI graph as an object).
Add a kind branch to graphFor() in server/index.ts .
Add a page in src/pages/ and an entry in APPS in src/catalog.ts .
Expose it to agents: a body builder in mcp/bodies.ts , a parity case in mcp/bodies.check.ts , and a tool in mcp/server.ts .
The contest asks entrants to name every model and tool they combine. This is the full list, taken from server/models.ts and the graph builders. Licenses are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md .
LTX-2.5 22B distilled transformer, video VAE, audio VAE and the x2 latent spatial upscaler.
Gemma 4 12B text encoder with the LTX projections (Google Gemma 4, packaged by Lightricks).
LTX-2.5 IC-LoRAs: Layout-to-Render (Stage), Ingredients (Cast), SDR-to-HDR and its scene embeddings (Finish in HDR), Alpha-Gen (Cutout), Water-Simulation (Flood), Day-To-Night (Nightfall), Clean-Plate (Empty the scene). The Cinemagraph LoRA (Living photo).
LTX-2.3 IC-LoRAs that run on LTX-2.5: Union Control (Mirror) and In/Outpainting (Object swap).
CrossView-Warp v2 IC-LoRA and node (Cseti), for Reshoot.
Community LoRAs by kabachuha for Effects: ltx23-pop, ltx2-inflate, ltx2-cakeify-v2, ltx2-handsquish, ltx2-disguise-drop and ltx2-eat-v2.
Gemma 3 12B (from the legacy ltx23 bundle) as the Scene planner when it is installed.
Qwen-Image with its VAE, Qwen-Image-Edit 2509 and the Qwen2.5-VL 7B text encoder (Alibaba Qwen).
Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 Lightning 8-step LoRAs (lightx2v), the Qwen-Edit-2509 Multiple-angles LoRA (dx8152).
Z-Image Turbo (Tongyi-MAI), its Qwen3 4B text encoder, the FLUX.1 VAE ( ae.safetensors , Black Forest Labs) and the Z-Image-Turbo Fun ControlNet Union (Alibaba PAI), for Stage look frames.
DWPose and the YOLOX-L person detector (Mirror body mode) and Depth Anything V2 Small (Mirror depth mode), through comfyui_controlnet_aux .
TRELLIS.2 4B with its shape and texture VAEs (Microsoft) and the DINOv3 ViT-L image encoder (Meta), for Object.
BiRefNet , for Remove background and Object.
SAM 3.1 (Meta), for steady and tracked mattes and Object swap.
SeedVR2 3B and 7B with its VAE (ByteDance Seed), for Upscale Redraw.
RIFE 4.7, for frame doubling and Director speed ramps.
FLUX.2 dev with its Mistral Small 3 text encoder, VAE and Turbo LoRA (Black Forest Labs, non-commercial).
MiniMax H3 FL2VA and Ref2VA with the Qwen3-VL 32B encoder, video and audio VAEs and the lightx2v turbo LoRAs (geo-restricted).
4x-UltraSharp (non-commercial), a second Sharpen model.
An Ollama model as the Scene planner fallback (gpt-oss 20B, Qwen3 30B or 8B, or Gemma 3 12B, whichever is installed).
A local whisper CLI for dialogue transcripts ( WHISPER_BIN ).
ComfyUI 0.38+, the Comfy SDK and comfy-api-proxy (Comfy Org).
Custom node packs: ComfyUI-LTXVideo, VideoHelperSuite, KJNodes, comfyui_controlnet_aux, ComfyUI-CrossViewWarp, ComfyUI-SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler and ComfyUI-Frame-Interpolation. ComfyUI's core GLSLShader node runs the era grade.
ffmpeg and ffprobe: the seam meter, HDR format checks, alpha clips and previews.
App: React, Vite, Fastify, SQLite (better-sqlite3), three.js, the MCP SDK, zod and ws.
OpenField is an independent project with its own name, design, copy and presets. Higgsfield and Comfy Org do not endorse it.
